normative_extracts.quote: The URLSearchParams interface defines utility methods to work with the query string of a URL.
pushState() adds a new entry to the browser's session history stack, while replaceState() modifies the current history entry without creating a new Back step.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Stores shareable view state (filters, pagination, tabs) in URL search params, choosing pushState for Back-navigable steps and replaceState for continuous edits.

production_failures.symptom: User must hit the Browser Back button 19 times to leave a search page
production_failures.root_cause: Every keystroke in the search input called history.pushState() instead of replaceState(), polluting the session history stack.
production_failures.mitigation: Use history.replaceState() for live search typing/slider scrubbing, and reserve pushState() for discrete commits like page changes or tab switches.

production_failures.symptom: Malicious or malformed ?page=-999&sort=invalid crashes the table component
production_failures.root_cause: Component read raw query strings from URLSearchParams without runtime schema parsing or fallback defaults.
production_failures.mitigation: Parse and clamp all URL search parameters through a strict schema validator (e.g., Zod) with safe defaults.
